newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran holds mediation talks between Sudan, Uganda.
newsitem.headline: Iran holds mediation talks between Sudan, Uganda.

text.p: Iran held talks on Tuesday with representatives from Sudan and Uganda to resolve border tensions between the two African countries, Tehran radio said.

It said the talks in Tehran aimed to follow up an Iran-brokered accord under which Sudan and Uganda, which accuse each other of supporting anti-government rebel groups, agreed in September to halt their activities in the border area.
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Hossein Sheikholeslam told the session he hoped Sudan and Uganda would agree to the setting up of an observer group to monitor the accord, the radio said.
Malawi, which has mediated in the past between Sudan and Uganda, also attended the talks, it said.
The delegations also met Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, who mediated the agreement, the radio added.
Sheikholeslam visited Uganda and Sudan last week to ease tensions between the two neighbours after Kampala said two Sudanese planes dropped bombs at army barracks in a Ugandan border town.
Khartoum denied the charge, saying its planes attacked Sudanese rebels inside Sudan.
